title: Coles CEO salary: how does it compare to the hourly-to-annual pay of a typical worker?
description: See how the coles ceo salary of $4.7 million stacks up against the annual pay of a worker on the National Minimum Wage, using the standard 38-hour week formula.
salarySummary: The coles ceo salary for 2023-24 was $4.7 million, while a full-time worker on the National Minimum Wage of $26.44 per hour earns about $52,254 per year (38 hours × 52 weeks).

faqs.q: What is the National Minimum Wage in Australia from July 2026?
faqs.a: The National Minimum Wage from 1 July 2026 is $26.44 per hour, or $1,004.90 per week for a 38-hour week. Casual employees receive an additional 25% loading, making it $33.05 per hour.

faqs.q: How does casual loading affect the annual pay calculation?
faqs.a: Casual loading of 25% is paid on top of the base hourly rate. For example, a casual on the National Minimum Wage earns $33.05 per hour. Their annual pay would be $33.05 × 38 × 52 = $65,318.80, before tax and super. Super is paid on top of the base rate plus loading.

bodyMarkdown:
## Converting hourly rates to annual pay

Whether you're negotiating a salary, comparing job offers, or just curious about what your hourly rate means over a full year, the standard conversion is straightforward: multiply your hourly rate by the number of hours you work per week, then multiply by 52 weeks. For most full-time roles, we assume a 38-hour week, which is the ordinary hours benchmark used by the Fair Work Ombudsman and the Australian Bureau of Statistics.

For example, the National Minimum Wage from 1 July 2026 is $26.44 per hour. A full-time employee on that rate earns:

$26.44 × 38 hours × 52 weeks = $52,254.40 per year (before tax and super).

That works out to $1,004.90 per week, or $2,009.80 per fortnight. You can use [the timesheet](/) to run your own numbers, adjusting for your actual hours.

## The coles ceo salary in perspective

To put the scale of executive pay into context, consider the coles ceo salary. According to a parliamentary submission and media reports, Coles CEO Leah Weckert earned $4.7 million in 2023-24, her first full year in the role. That is up from $3.3 million the previous year and includes a fixed compensation package of $2 million per annum (including superannuation).

If we apply the same hourly conversion logic to the coles ceo salary, dividing $4.7 million by 38 hours and 52 weeks gives an implied hourly rate of roughly $2,378. But executive remuneration typically includes bonuses, long-term incentives, and equity, so the comparison is not like-for-like with a wage earner's hourly rate.

## Award rates and enterprise agreements

Not all workers are on the National Minimum Wage. Many are covered by awards or enterprise agreements that set higher minimum rates. For instance, the Coles Retail Agreement 2024 (an enterprise agreement) lists a Level 1 team member rate of $25.27 per hour – slightly below the National Minimum Wage, which shows that some agreements may lag behind the statutory minimum. Always check the applicable award or agreement for your industry.

Casual employees receive a 25% loading on top of their base rate. For a casual on the National Minimum Wage, that means $33.05 per hour. Their annual pay would be $33.05 × 38 × 52 = $65,318.80. The casual loading compensates for not receiving paid leave entitlements.

## Superannuation is paid on top

Under the Superannuation Guarantee, employers must contribute 12% of ordinary earnings (from 1 July 2026) into your super fund. This is paid on top of your gross pay, up to the maximum contribution base of $270,830 per year. So a full-time worker on the National Minimum Wage would receive an additional $6,270.53 in super contributions annually. You can learn more about [super and packaging](/topics/super-and-packaging).

## Tax and the Medicare levy

Once you have your annual gross figure, you need to estimate tax. The 2026–27 resident tax rates are:

- Nil on the first $18,200
- 15% on income from $18,201 to $45,000
- 30% on income from $45,001 to $135,000
- 37% on income from $135,001 to $190,000
- 45% on income over $190,000

Plus the Medicare levy of 2% of taxable income (with possible reductions for low-income earners, using the 2025–26 single thresholds as a guide).

For a worker earning $52,254 (National Minimum Wage), the estimated tax would be:

- Tax-free: $18,200
- Taxable at 15%: $34,054 → $5,108.10
- Medicare levy: $1,045.08
- Total tax: $6,153.18
- After-tax income: $46,100.82

This is an estimate only. It does not include the Medicare levy surcharge, HELP repayments, or salary sacrifice arrangements. For a more detailed breakdown, see our [take-home pay](/topics/take-home) guide.

## Using the conversion tool

Our [the timesheet](/) lets you enter your base hourly rate and optionally add casual loading. It then calculates your weekly, fortnightly, and annual gross pay, plus estimated tax and super. The tool assumes a 38-hour week unless you change the hours. Remember that the annual figure is hourly × hours per week × 52, and it assumes the same rate every week with no unpaid overtime, penalty rates, or allowances.

## Summary

Understanding the gap between the coles ceo salary and a typical worker's pay helps put your own earnings in context. The coles ceo salary of $4.7 million is roughly 50 times the average full-time worker's earnings of around $108,000 (based on ABS Average Weekly Earnings of $2,083.70 per week). But for most people, the conversion from hourly to annual is a simple calculation that can clarify job offers and budget planning. Use our tools and guides to get a clearer picture of your own pay.
